questions.prompt: Every device taps into one long backbone cable with a terminator at each end.
Each device connects to exactly two neighbors, forming a closed loop.
Every device has its own cable to one central switch.
Every router is linked directly to every other router.
Exactly two devices share one dedicated link.
Several star networks hang off a core in levels, like branches.
Cheapest to wire, but one break anywhere takes everything down and the fault is hard to find.
A token circulates, and only the device holding it may send.
Most reliable, because traffic can always take another path, but it's expensive and the redundancy adds traffic.
Fast and easy to troubleshoot, but if the hub fails, everyone is cut off.
Works well across long distances and big campuses, but it's complex to configure and costs more.
Good quality and collision-free, but every device added slows the trip around.
